slides.say: a and b are positive integers. Given: two to the power of a, times three to the power of b, is equal to a hundred eight. What is a minus b?

So the left side is written in primes, and the right side is a plain number. The idea is to write a hundred eight in primes too, and match. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, breaking and matching, and then dividing down.

[short pause] Why does matching work? A number breaks into primes in only one way. Wherever you start the factor tree, you end with the same primes. For example, eighteen. Two times nine breaks into two, three, three, and three times six breaks into three, two, three. The same primes, just in another order.

So if both sides are the same number, they must have the same twos and the same threes. Now a hundred eight. It's four times twenty-seven, because four times twenty-five is a hundred, and four times two is eight. Four is two squared, and twenty-seven is three cubed.

The exponents a and b count the copies of two and three. Since both sides represent the same number, those copy counts must match. So two to the power of a, times three to the power of b, is two squared times three cubed. The twos match, so a is two. The threes match, so b is three.
at: So two to the power of a

slides.say: Now careful, they ask for a minus b, not b minus a. Two minus three is negative one, so choice number three is our answer.
at: choice number three is our answer

slides.say: Choice number one, positive one, is what you get when you swap a and b. Choice number four, five, is a plus b. And two is just a.

[pause] Each exact division by two removes one copy of two. Counting those divisions will therefore tell us the exponent a. I divide by two as long as I can, and count. A hundred eight over two is fifty-four. Fifty-four over two is twenty-seven. Twenty-seven is odd, so no more twos. Two halvings, so a is two.
Then the threes. Twenty-seven over three is nine, nine over three is three, and three over three is one. Three times, so b is three.
a minus b, two minus three, negative one. Choice number three again. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
